- NEW [filter] Sideways filter: do not trade when the 1/5-min EMAs (9/20) are flat (not sloped up) and price is chopping after the squeeze; indifference candles/reversal candles have no meaning in a sideways range. His example: $55k day, trade legs up only, no trades in post-flag chop where MAs flatten. (1:00-7:35)

Entry = first candle to make a new high after the pullback; stop = low of pullback; target = break through the prior high. Example 6.00 -> 8.50 (ran to 11, then 12). Found via high-of-day momentum scanner alert, then wait for 1st pullback. (8:35-12:11)

A dramatic topping tail with a huge seller on Level 2 in the way can be acted on before close; one giant rejection candle (e.g. spike to 3.50 then back) can "ruin the chart" for the rest of the day. ## LNDd7rf-9FU · 2025 · How to Read Technical Indicators on Candlestick Charts
read: 100% (teaching class; most content restates known EMA/VWAP/MACD/5-pillar rules)
- NEW [setup] Multi-timeframe alignment: a 1-min pullback to the 20 EMA coincides with the 5-min chart pulling back to its 9 EMA (two small red 5-min candles after a green one with a wick), i.e. a "picture perfect" 5-min bull flag; the 1-min pattern that "broke" the 9 EMA is still valid at the 20 EMA when the 5-min is at its 9 EMA. 5-min 9 EMA = nine 5-min candles (45 min) so it is a different level than the 1-min 9. (23:00-26:00)
- NEW [setup] Candle rhythm: charts tend to repeat their own cadence (e.g. 2-3 green, 2 red, 3 green, 2 red), so a first-candle-to-new-high off the 9 EMA is expected to give about 2-3 candles of follow-through if the prior legs did. (6:03)
- NEW [exit] Bollinger band exit (settings 20, 2 st.dev.): a candle almost fully outside the upper band = reversal/take-profit signal for a long; stronger when stacked with RSI(14, lines 20/80) overbought, a topping tail/shooting star/doji after long-body candles, and a large L2 seller (example: 200,000-share seller at the high of $0.60). Stock can stay outside bands for a long time on a strong catalyst (example 50c to $5 outside the band the whole way, many halts), so it is a "take profit / do not add" cue, not a short signal. Short-side version: scale in cautiously, add full size on final flush red candle outside the lower band. (51:01-58:01)
- NEW [filter] Volume profile (visible range) point of control (POC): trade above POC bullish, below bearish; prior-session POC acts as resistance at the open (example POC $8.40: stock ran into it and was rejected); after a front-side spike POC moves up with the new volume and stays above price = upside resistance on any later rally; POC useless on the front side, useful for timing deeper pullbacks, especially POC near the 200 MA or VWAP. Breakout above the POC after a pullback was his best trade of that day (day total $12,894). Stocks that previously popped then dipped have few trapped sellers above the old high ("hasn't traded up there in a long time"). (58:01-1:06:01)
- NEW [filter] 200 EMA on the daily is resistance when below and support when above; only breaks intraday on a very strong catalyst (example: US rare-earth producer breaking the daily 200 on the tariff-hike news). Pre-flight checklist before every trade: daily 200 position and room, 9/20 EMA position, intraday 200, VWAP, MACD open, volume green > red; "everything has to check out", he spends most time talking himself out of trades. Intraday ribbon 9 > 20 > 200: when the 9 crosses below the 20 "stock is not going to work anymore". (16:00-18:00, 28:00-32:00)
- NEW [filter] MACD crossovers are slow to repair: after a large negative cross it can take 15-20 minutes or hours to flip positive, so a big cross + failed double top (cannot break previous high) + RSI still overbought = unwind, no longs. MACD settings 12/26/9 on the close, never customised ("be the same as everyone else"); signal computed only at candle close; he keeps both lines visible (not histogram-only) to judge how far above the signal it is. He learned "only trade when MACD positive" in the last bear market (gave back profit buying the curl after the cross in cold markets). (33:02-37:03, 57:00)
- STAT Ross accuracy over the previous 30 days (as of this 2025 recording): 76%; quotes 70-75% as a good-trader range. (1:01)

## YZ5nvP7DnQQ · 2024 · TOP 5 Day Trading Mistakes YOU NEED TO KNOW!!
read: 100%
- NEW [filter] "Shadow Theory" for daily-chart resistance mapping: any prior high/level that a LATER candle's range has traded through (broke) is invalidated and must not be used as resistance/target; only levels not yet broken by subsequent price count. Procedure: scan "left and up" from current price, start with the largest/most obvious candle highs, mark the next unbroken candle high above price, skip any high that a later candle exceeded (e.g. a high broken "on the very next day" is gone). Target = nearest unbroken level, not an old level behind a big candle (0:37-6:18)
- NEW [filter] Daily "window" = zone left by one very large candle (not a gap) where no unbroken prior highs exist above price -> clean air; e.g. levels 7.96 -> next unbroken high 12.08 -> all-time high 26.60 on OCEA example; a break over the first level with hold = target next unbroken level (4:28-6:01)
- NEW [filter] Exception to Shadow Theory: a double top (price repeatedly rejected at the same level, e.g. ~$9.50 touched twice by candles) stays valid resistance even though a candle later traded through it; also whole/half-dollar levels at the top of a move (3, 4, 4.40, 9.50) are marked, small gradual-descent highs are ignored as insignificant (7:04-9:00)

Tier 1 (S&P500/Dow) >$3 = 5%. Examples: close ~$1.20 -> 20c band; close ~$12 -> 10% band (halt level ~$13.22 vs price $12.2) (9:00-11:30)
- NEW [execution] LULD reference price = average price of the last 5 minutes, recomputed every 30 s only if the new reference differs >=1% from the current one; a halt triggers only if price sits AT the band for 15 seconds (else band moves and no halt). Slow grinds rarely halt; instant spikes do. Band is computable in real time (needs L2 data feed showing LULD levels) (12:30-14:31)
- NEW [execution] Halt-imminent tell: price at LULD level with bid = ask (crossed/locked market), single seller at the LULD price and a stack of buyers, only sell orders executing -> halt within seconds (16:32-17:31)
- NEW [execution] Resumption timing: volatility halt (LULD/LP on Nasdaq, "M" on NYSE/AMEX) = exactly 5 min from time of LAST TRADE (to the second, e.g. halted 10:20:18 -> 10:25:18); if order imbalance remains, extends in 5-min increments (10,15,20...). Pre-resume quote on Nasdaq shows indicated resumption price (e.g. halt 1.84, indicated 1.90 -> 1.92 -> 2.18 -> 2.24 as a 6,500-sh bid appeared; can revert to 1.84) (19:00-22:30)
- NEW [execution] NYSE/AMEX-listed stocks show NO indicated resumption quote during halt; Nasdaq does. He is more cautious on NYSE/AMEX-listed small caps (also see T1 below) (23:31, 28:31)
- NEW [setup] Resumption-quote read: halt UP + indicated higher resumption = bullish (hold/add; his normal case); halt UP but indicated LOWER resumption = unusual, be cautious / place sell near breakeven; halt DOWN usually resumes lower; flat resumption (e.g. 11.87/11.87) = neutral (24:00-25:00)
- NEW [setup] Dip-and-rip mechanism: beginners place multiple sell orders in the halt (on easy-to-borrow names these flip them short on resumption), producing an initial flush at resumption then squeeze back up; he waits for the dip then buys the rip (not buying pre-resumption) (22:30-23:31)
- NEW [regime] Many LULD circuit-breaker halts in one day = indicator of strong momentum/hot market (3:31)
- NEW [filter] Back-to-back halts (up then down, repeated) are common on sub-$0.75 stocks (15c band) and slow momentum -> undesirable (25:30)
- NEW [filter] Halt codes: T1 = pending news; if COMPANY requested it, news is usually bad (good news is released without halting); T12 = SEC/exchange suspension (can last weeks-months, worst); NYSE/AMEX more likely to issue T1 halt on a huge no-news spike (e.g. +1,000%); resumes only after company statement ("not aware of any undisclosed material change"), can take hours, typically resumes ~50% lower (G: "50% the current price") (26:01-28:31)
